invariants.claim: One conditional successor publishes a prepared transition
scenarios: Competing prepared successors
Acknowledgement lost after append

invariants.claim: Current grants and activation generation fence new publication and receipt disclosure
scenarios: Revoke or replace owner between prepare and commit
Retry committed work after read revocation
invariants.limits: Authorization does not prove application computation or undo external effects.

invariants.claim: Mutations, consumed input and outputs have one visibility decision
scenarios: Stale resource revisions and private rollback
Restart before/after conditional append
Generated captured-view turns publish one KV value and input progress together
invariants.limits: Bounded state-v1 projection; growing publication has separate GROWTH invariants and real disk proofs.

invariants.claim: Exact retry preserves one durable outcome and unknown is not rejection
scenarios: Lost accepted response followed by exact retry
Malformed reply and host loss
Independent same-principal native handles race conflicting and identical frozen requests
invariants.limits: Response allocation after acceptance is enumerated through the real ABI response/status path with a deterministic transport; real HTTP/host loss and same-principal multi-handle races use disk-backed service proofs. Public SDK adapters remain M11 work; shared obligations are in tests/verification/sdk.json.

invariants.claim: Expiry and settlement closure cannot be reopened by late work or old recovery state
scenarios: Uncertain time at admission cutoff
Paused dispatch and late reconciliation
invariants.limits: Validation occurs at compared journal tail; physical external dispatch may occur later.

invariants.claim: Recovery restores decisions without running handlers or redispatching effects
scenarios: SIGKILL and WAL recovery
Checkpoint plus trimmed tail
invariants.limits: Process kill is not host power loss; legacy checkpoint includes the whole bounded catalog.

invariants.claim: Pressure never silently deletes accepted work and control reserve permits closure
scenarios: Admission ceiling with outstanding input
Real ENOSPC followed by revocation and restart
invariants.limits: Legacy derived reserve and separately configured growing reserve have finite real ENOSPC proofs. Their owned ext4 fixtures preallocate physical headroom; nodes do not provision it automatically. GROWTH-11 covers growing service/Station quota semantics. No arbitrary workload worst-case sizing claim.

invariants.claim: Cancellation and disposal join owned native work without manufacturing rollback
scenarios: Cancel host await during native operation
Child/port failure and malformed framing
invariants.limits: Finite target-language schedules, not exhaustive interleaving or non-Linux qualification.

invariants.claim: Complete query bytes retain exact schema, values, nulls and source revision
scenarios: Independent PyArrow and wide integers
Missing fragments and consumer restart
invariants.limits: Bounded synchronous results only; paged multi-batch execution remains unqualified.

invariants.claim: Incremental query limits and ordered aggregates span batches without silently truncating source or output
scenarios: 70 rows, variable partitions, global filter/limit, null and exact integer aggregates
Signed overflow across page boundaries despite a cancelling later value
Plan/basis/ordinal rejection, allocation/output/cancellation faults and deterministic retry
Independent PyArrow segments and Python progress/fingerprint encoding
invariants.limits: Pure synchronous bounded steps only; durable Station capture, policy, staging and consumer restart remain integration gates. Digests do not prove honest caller computation.

invariants.claim: Incremental result staging cannot advance sealed source progress or expose a partial job as captured
scenarios: 70-row private capture with fresh turns, lost private proposals, duplicate/future continuations and corruption
41-row real capture, lost stage/seal replies, two caller/node/provider replacements; one-page first recovery and selectable final cache
Independent PyArrow bytes and ordered segment digest-chain validation
Policy change and poisoned source read cannot publish; explicit fresh closure retains evidence
invariants.limits: Capture slice only. Result delivery, consumer completeness and acknowledgement remain integration work; no full-store, GC or production throughput claim. Job and source share a resource.

invariants.claim: Provider recovery and upgrades cannot grant ownership or redirect durable work
scenarios: Lost provider create/update response
Fresh activation after pod replacement
invariants.limits: Only Zig workers qualified in the reference substrate; native tests do not establish sandbox isolation.

invariants.claim: Inspection preserves current authorization, revision boundaries and explicit gaps
scenarios: Read revoked between pages
Resource/view expiry and history gap
Generated view expiry, uncertain time, rollback and current resource grants
invariants.limits: Board is private-boundary inspection; the legacy view is a full bounded resource copy.

invariants.claim: Diagnostic pressure cannot stall authority or expose application credentials
scenarios: Stalled log pipe on one CPU
Lost HTTP acknowledgement retains receipt semantics
invariants.limits: Bounded diagnostics may be dropped; they are not durable authority.

invariants.claim: Accepted bounded wire values preserve canonical identity and owned bytes
scenarios: Malformed/truncated signed JSON under fixed workspace
Owned binary frame and exact correlation roundtrip
Allocation enumeration through parse and canonical output
invariants.limits: Finite corpus and bounded Zig fuzz budget; no claim that a roundtrip replaces independent canonical vectors or Arrow readers.

invariants.claim: Immutable roots preserve old values independently of resident cache and root-journal trimming

invariants.claim: A growing control root atomically retains mailbox admission and exact retry evidence beyond legacy process/principal counts

Prepared root loses to revocation
Acknowledgement lost after root publication
Historical retry after later acceptance
Recovery without staging pages

invariants.claim: Growing state turns atomically publish bounded mutations, progress, captured outputs and closed views without loading the whole resource

scenarios: More than four resources, thirty-two rows and four retained views
Rejected destination after staged rows preserves live root
Current resource rights on historical receipt disclosure
Expiry through lifetime-owner dependency graph cannot be rebound away
invariants.limits: In-memory injected page/journal proof. Transport, background terminal projection, quota reserves and real service/Station remain unqualified.

invariants.claim: Bounded paged reads preserve their declared state basis without retaining stale permission or ownership

scenarios: Captured old resource version versus later writer commit
Current grants, ownership, deadline and clock uncertainty
Bounded empty filtered page with a non-null continuation

Missing pages and stale catalog cuts reject explicitly
invariants.limits: Internal signed engine queries with injected storage/time. No HTTP/SDK/provider proof, generalized historical querying or concurrent service load qualification.

invariants.claim: Indexed delivery and bounded settlement preserve order, retry identity and permanent closure without scanning retained work
invariants.profile: transit-v3 development work slice; not running service
scenarios: Independent routes and stale prepared admission after revocation
Lost delivery and observation acknowledgements
Retired caller with an authorized external attempt
Finite turn settlement, late-result rejection and permanent expiry
invariants.limits: Injected storage/time; no HTTP connector, automatic maintenance, real provider or service integration evidence.

invariants.claim: Published growing authority roots recover through disk restart and opted-in root-history compaction without materializing all retained state

Failure before publication and acknowledgement loss after publication
Captured version and exact receipt survive restart and opted-in root checkpoint/trim
Uncommitted trim intent and missing pages reject; retained outboxes/mailboxes remain
invariants.limits: Trusted test clock and injected acknowledgement loss at the real journal boundary. No service/SDK/Station integration, provider cluster, quota/control reserve or throughput qualification. Root history retains its latest complete head; pages are not reclaimed.

invariants.claim: An explicit growing service profile supports signed bounded caller reads and atomic turns without exposing raw storage or executing application handlers
invariants.profile: transit-v3 development service; legacy launcher defaults preserved
scenarios: Wide caller principal and sixty-four rows with bounded point/paged reads
Wrong realm, mixed revisions, page holes and nonadvancing cursors reject
Accepted malformed receipt remains uncertain across caller/node/provider restart

Single-CPU HTTP concurrency and no legacy-route fallback
Activation helper reads bounded captured keys and freezes owned retry material
Session resolves named associations without materializing the catalog
invariants.limits: No Station/foreign binding support, runtime binding, migration, load qualification or quota/control reserve claim. Host synchronized clock is a deployment premise.

invariants.claim: Bounded background suggestions revalidate before publication and physical trimming requires current control authority and committed opt-in

Retained bytes, independent state and authorized external attempts survive terminal-source cleanup and disk restart

invariants.limits: Full process/resource sweep cost still grows with retained metadata. No page GC, due-time index, sweep-lag SLO, full-store control reserve or multi-maintainer performance claim. Physical work authorized before revocation may finish later.

invariants.claim: Growing Station private turns read bounded captured keys and retain call semantics without a whole-resource snapshot
scenarios: Point access beyond 32 Table rows without materializing the resource

Cross-resource atomic rollback and read-your-own writes
Wide observer identity and authenticated timeout/reply closure
Legacy wait versions reject growing records and vice versa
Real retained calls and Table rows survive caller/node/provider restart beyond 32 keys
Caught malformed state response cannot publish private work or a failure marker
Lost accepted turn response retries exact signed bytes without rerunning a handler
Fresh ownership fences an old prepared turn and skips committed initialization
Typed bounded Table pages preserve order across negative and extreme keys without entering a neighboring Table

Retained source helpers register proposal dependencies and poison caught failures

PID scope and current admin permission independently enforced

New mailbox input can queue behind a failed head without bypassing its ordered retry

invariants.claim: Retained read versions publish atomically with progress, survive activation replacement and never retain authority
invariants.profile: transit-v3 retained read version development capability
scenarios: Existing signed command/query digests remain unchanged
Private staging and invalid release publish no version or progress
Lost accepted retention reply recovers one receipt
Read pre-mutation rows after caller/node/provider restart with one resident page

Missing captured page is unavailable, never an empty result
Explicit release is terminal and cannot be undone by retry
Declared retained read dependencies reject stale publication and reauthorize historical receipts
Live versions survive physical authority-prefix trim and provider restart
invariants.limits: No resumable Station/Fuze result capture, quota accounting or page garbage collection. Catalog roots may retain unrelated physical pages. Disk provider proof checks authority-prefix trim while preserving immutable page storage.

invariants.claim: A growing control root refuses new admission before an explicit journal reserve, while revocation, retry, termination, delivery, observation, checkpoint and output-free turns keep draining and closing existing work through it
invariants.profile: transit-v3 development control slice; not running service
scenarios: Admission ceiling with outstanding input, reserve exhaustion and restart
Signed capabilities query reports ceiling/reserve headroom before, at and past the ceiling
Real ENOSPC, physical reserve release, retained rows/receipts, backlog drain, checkpoint/trim and SIGKILL recovery
Station pending view and accepted backlog survive public quota refusal, restart and reserve exhaustion
invariants.limits: Finite single-authority capacity profile: 96 admission and 96 control positions on owned 2 GiB ext4 with a preallocated 1 GiB physical reserve. Separate one-CPU Station service proof uses 24 plus 4 positions. Bounds are deployment policy; no automatic physical provisioning or arbitrary-scale reserve guarantee.

invariants.claim: Growing result segments are accepted strictly in order, receiver-issued credit never exceeds durably stored segments, the sender never exceeds its observed credit window, and acknowledgement never precedes full receipt

scenarios: Duplicate/retried segment after a lost credit grant or acknowledgement is inert
Sender blocked at the credit window until a grant is observed
Acknowledgement only reachable once every segment is durably received
invariants.limits: Type/safety-only TLC check of the abstract credit protocol; no guard mutants or Zig trace replay yet, unlike Authority.tla. Fragmentation below one segment, digest/schema verification and durable KV encoding are exercised by test::unit, not this model.

invariants.claim: Offered public load preserves every admission, exact receipt and row update across disk restart while scoped revocation progresses
scenarios: Fixed-cache growth across 64/256/1024 retained rows and 69 associations
Independently scheduled signed admissions with generator queueing and control latency
Uniform and hot-key drain, exact receipts, row digest and revocation through node/provider restart
invariants.limits: Finite loopback samples with 48 offered operations, bounded producer workers and disk/S3 storage. No production SLO, horizontal capacity, power-loss or object-store-crash guarantee.

invariants.claim: Complete single-Table SQL lowers to the existing typed plan without silently dropping clauses or truncating unbounded selection

Exact plan codec and independent PyArrow results over 70-row sources
Owned bounded parsing, trailing statements, schema/type/limit exclusions
Compiled aggregates retain ordered overflow, cancellation and source fencing
invariants.limits: Declared syntax subset only; no PostgreSQL execution-equivalence claim, SQL endpoint, catalog access, writes or optimizer rewrite.

invariants.claim: Named specification rewrites preserve ordered projection/selection and stated first-error behavior under explicit factorization premises

scenarios: Total predicate reordering and projection pruning
Fallible predicate pushdown through total projection
Unchanged downstream consumer preserves errors
Required theorem and axiom inventory rejects incomplete proof
invariants.limits: No optimizer enabled; authority, allocation, cancellation and partial projections are outside the model. Limit pushdown and checked-sum reassociation are not claimed.

invariants.claim: Public Table queries preserve exact submission, bounded behavior admission, source/schema identity and current result-read authority

scenarios: Lost admission receipt retries the exact signed request
Worker SIGKILL requires fresh ownership and resumes captured work
Busy admission and mismatched schemas never create an accepted result
Incomplete results are unreadable; explicit cancellation remains distinct
Revocation denies new reads and clears the remembered CLI query
Revocation after an actually received segment denies disclosure until explicit reauthorization
invariants.limits: One configured Table/requester per principal; no SQL writes, KV/Document adapters, offline result copies or power-loss proof. Transport inbox quota remains a separate deployment constraint.

invariants.claim: Board keeps inspection read-only and exposes separately credentialed Table queries with one draft/result and current-authority disclosure
invariants.profile: M13 growing Board and optional public query v1
scenarios: Current identity rejects a widened inspection grant and stale atlas cuts
Default query-disabled configuration and malformed/arbitrary query ingress refusal
Opaque frozen retries and typed int64 cells preserve exact values
Canvas/Browse changes preserve draft/result without new execution
Open workspace clears protected data after read revocation without browser persistence
Frozen cancellation and source retirement remain distinct from successful completion
invariants.limits: One configured Table/principal; eight-item catalog pages, no global metrics, default legacy inspection unchanged. No per-human delegation, KV/Document query, power-loss or production capacity claim.

invariants.claim: Large immutable records have one final visibility decision, bounded staging and resumable terminal cleanup
scenarios: Independent commitment fixtures and malformed descriptors
Quota reservation, conflicting identity and private rollback
Worker SIGKILL before and after publication; node/store restart with one resident page
Lost append/publication/cleanup receipts and exact retry
Stale ownership, read revocation after a prefix, expired view and released retained source
Interrupted cleanup resumes without reusing identities; historical source survives current deletion
invariants.limits: Single authority, disk Ursula, 64 KiB record and 41 additional 32-byte records. No host power-loss, production throughput, automatic jobs, physical erasure, CRDT, SDK or widened query claim.

invariants.claim: Immutable segments, exact request intent coverage and terminal availability compose without exceeding a turn budget
scenarios: Four-mutation segment publication, conflicting identities, quota refusal and rollback
Retirement rejects a cursor after a returned prefix even with an old source
Ready request coverage creates one effect intent; binding rejects different coverage
Independent HTTP/TLS peers, binary chunking and trailers, omissions and current hostname verification
Dropped, truncated, ambiguous, oversized and stalled responses; no hidden redirects, retries or ambient proxies
Actual worker disk recovery, lost seal/dispatch/observation replies, current read revocation, entered-generation refusal and SIGKILL after remote application
TLS worker binds credential versions/header scope, rejects changed numeric destinations and replays after credential removal
Public caller admission with immutable request references and exact method/target/header scope; optional read associations keep reconciliation independent of caller lifetime
Caller termination after remote application, worker/node/store replacement, original attempt closure and retired output destination without replacement activation
Native/port HTTP fixtures, scoped publication actions and validated calls; one owned replay reader, prefix revocation, sticky failure, stale IDs and allocation rollback

Installed Python, Node, Rust, Ruby, C, C++, Java, .NET, Erlang and Elixir HTTP callers: bounded upload with fresh ownership after host loss, binary TLS and Unicode/duplicate headers, correlated reply, owned replay without credentials and joined local stop/disposal
invariants.limits: Finite HTTP/1.1 worker over disk Ursula: one public root call per provisioned connector PID, 64 KiB request profile, 1,027-byte worker response; independent transport response 16,387 bytes. Explicit controller retry/redirect/status/cancel and all ten public HTTP SDKs are qualified. Public followup/release conveniences, Board, launchers and hosted costs remain M15 work. Numeric IPv4 endpoint, identity encoding; TLS close-delimited bodies rejected.
